purpose: The vocabulary of bracketed tokens the engine-form formatter (src/voice/engine-form.js) may remove or pass through. Work order W7 rev 2.1 sections 2 and 3, amended by W8 sections 2 and 3. A bracketed token that is neither listed here NOR tag-shaped is CONTENT and is never transformed.
matching: Two rules, and the class decides which applies. CLASS A is matched by MEMBERSHIP only: a channel marker is enumerated, never shape-matched, because a shape rule cannot tell [OUTPUT] from a quoted word. A Class A token matches when it is equal to the entry's token or one of its variants after asterisks and underscores are removed from both (so [**warm**] is [warm], and [[TRAVELRESEARCH_FORM]] is [[TRAVEL_RESEARCH_FORM]], the form the incremental route's markdown stripper produces). Comparison is case-sensitive unless the entry sets case_insensitive. An entry with scope 'line' removes the rest of its line as well (a control line). CLASS B is matched by SHAPE, not by membership: a single-bracket token of one to four lower-case words separated by a space or by a comma and a space is a cue, whatever words it contains. Case is discriminating, so [warm] is a cue and [Warm] is content. Three exclusions decide before the shape rule, so a token is content even when it is tag-shaped: a subscript context (a[i], arr[idx] -- the character before the bracket is a letter, digit, underscore or close bracket), a reference or checkbox form ([1], [^3], [], [ ], [x]), and a Class A name in any case. Content spans (fenced blocks, inline code, [label](target) links) are decided before any token is classified, so a cue inside one is content whatever it says.

B.name: prosody and register cues
B.rule: stripped on the Kokoro path always; on the ElevenLabs path passed through when the user's tag switch is on, stripped otherwise. Matched by SHAPE (see matching), not by membership.
B.confirmed: The tokens below are the set whose behaviour has actually been observed rather than inferred. They are RETAINED here because Kokoro has no tag vocabulary, so a bracketed token that reaches it is read aloud; on that path this list and the shape rule have the same effect, and the list is the documented safe set. The list is NOT the matching rule: the engine's vocabulary is wider than this and is maintained by the vendor, so a new cue does not need a file edit and a deploy.
